cues.zh: 在第一集中，也就是现在已经上线的那一集，我们和Hank Green进行了交谈。如果你能试试看，我将非常感激，链接在描述下方。

cues.en: Trains are expensive.
cues.zh: 火车很贵。

cues.en: So expensive in fact that on three of the most traveled routes in three countries, New York to Washington in The US, Edinburgh to London in The UK, and Paris De Leon in France, they're pretty much the same price as the plane. These routes start at $49.30
cues.zh: 贵到什么程度呢？在三个国家最繁忙的三条线路上——美国的纽约到华盛顿、英国的 Edinburgh 到伦敦、法国的巴黎到里昂——火车票价几乎和机票一样。这些线路的火车票起价分别是 49.30 美元、

cues.en: pounds and €30 respectively on the train and $52.13
cues.zh: 英镑和 30 欧元，而机票起价是 52.13 美元、

cues.en: pounds and €53
cues.zh: 英镑和 53

cues.en: on the plane. On a longer route like New York to Chicago, the difference is even more pronouncedfifty
cues.zh: 欧元。在更长的线路上，比如纽约到芝加哥，差距就更明显了——机票 59

cues.en: nine dollars for the plane, 108
cues.zh: 美元，火车 108

cues.en: for the train. And that's keeping in mind that trains are subsidized or government run-in almost every country while airlines are highly profitable commercial enterprises.
cues.zh: 美元。而且别忘了，几乎所有国家的火车都有补贴或由政府运营，而航空公司则是高利润的商业企业。

cues.en: The planes flying between DC and New York are $49,000,000
cues.zh: 华盛顿和纽约之间飞行的飞机是4900万美元的

cues.en: machines while the trains traveling the route cost no more than 10,000,000 total. The plane has to burn 1.7
cues.zh: 机器，而沿途行驶的火车总成本不超过1000万美元。飞机每飞行一英里要燃烧1.7

cues.en: gallons of fuel per mile flown while the train relies on clean electric power. All this therefore begs the question,
cues.zh: 加仑燃料，而火车依靠清洁电力。因此，这一切引出了一个问题：

cues.en: why are trains so expensive?
cues.zh: 为什么火车如此昂贵？

cues.en: Now, I mentioned that fares between DC and New York start at $49
cues.zh: 现在，我提到华盛顿和纽约之间的票价起价为49美元

cues.en: but that's far from the average price, dollars 73.
cues.zh: 但这远非平均价格，平均为73美元。

cues.en: Let's look at the expenses that go into that fare.
cues.zh: 我们来看看这张票价里包含哪些费用。

cues.en: The single largest expense for Amtrak is staffing. Trains require a lot of people to operate. 85,000
cues.zh: Amtrak 最大的单项支出是人员开支。列车运营需要大量人手。8.5万

cues.en: passengers journey on Amtrak daily, but for that Amtrak employs 20,000
cues.zh: 名乘客每天乘坐 Amtrak，但为此 Amtrak 雇了 2万

cues.en: people.
cues.zh: 人。

cues.en: Meaning that daily,
cues.zh: 也就是说，每天

cues.en: Amtrak requires one employee for every four passengers.
cues.zh: Amtrak 每四名乘客就需要一名员工。

cues.en: On top of that, the majority of those working for Amtrak are highly specialized
cues.zh: 除此之外，Amtrak 的大多数员工都是高度专业化的

cues.en: unionized workers who demand high salaries.
cues.zh: 工会工人，要求高薪。

cues.en: Amtrak's financial reports tell us that they spend $105,000
cues.zh: Amtrak的财务报告告诉我们，他们每人花费105,000美元

cues.en: per employee, but that's not to say that everyone at Amtrak is making 6 figures. Taxes and benefits typically cost an employer 30 to 40% of a salary so the actual average salary for an Amtrak employee is around $75,000
cues.zh: 但这并不是说Amtrak的每个人都赚六位数。税收和福利通常占雇主支付的工资的30%到40%，所以Amtrak员工的实际平均工资大约是75,000美元

cues.en: These salary costs are so high that they account for over a third of the ticket price between DC and New York, dollars 25.82
cues.zh: 这些工资成本如此之高，以至于它们占了华盛顿和纽约之间票价的三分之一以上，总计25.82美元

cues.en: total.
cues.zh: 总计。

cues.en: The cost of employees is so high for train operators largely because trains are so slow. For a flight from DC to New York, an airline would only have to pay employees an hour of work while Amtrak has to pay their employees for three and a half hours of work. The difference is even more striking on the long haul routesChicago
cues.zh: 对火车运营商来说，员工成本之所以如此之高，很大程度上是因为火车太慢了。从DC飞往纽约的航班，航空公司只需支付员工一小时的工作时间，而Amtrak却要支付员工三个半小时的工作时间。在长途路线上，这种差距更加惊人——比如从芝加哥

cues.en: to Los Angeles, for example. An airline would have to pay for four hours of work while Amtrak pays for forty four hours of work. In addition, trains have physical infrastructure to maintain along the journeythe rails.
cues.zh: 到洛杉矶。航空公司只需支付四小时的工作时间，而Amtrak要支付四十四小时的工作时间。此外，火车在旅途中还有实体基础设施要维护——铁轨。

cues.en: Airlines also have infrastructure to pay for on each endthe airports but between those they just use the Sky, which is free. Amtrak only owns seven thirty miles of those 21,000
cues.zh: 航空公司也要为两端的机场基础设施付费，但两头之间他们只需用天空，那是免费的。Amtrak 在它使用的21000英里轨道中只拥有730英里，

cues.en: miles of track they use, but they still indirectly pay for the employees who maintain those 20,000 miles of rented track through the fees charged by the track owners for their use. The next largest cost for train operators is that of the trains themselves.
cues.zh: 但他们仍然通过轨道所有者收取的使用费，间接支付维护那两万英里租用轨道的员工工资。火车运营商的下一大成本是火车本身。

cues.en: Trains aren't that expensive compared to airplanes, but they still cost millions of dollars. The locomotive pulling the train from DC to New York costs $6,500,000
cues.zh: 和飞机相比，火车不算太贵，但仍要花费数百万美元。从华盛顿特区到纽约的火车头造价650万美元

cues.en: and then each one of the passenger cars costs an additional $400,000
cues.zh: 每节车厢还要额外花费40万美元

cues.en: With a seven car train, that works out to $9,400,000
cues.zh: 七节车厢的火车总价就是940万美元

cues.en: which accounts for $9.67
cues.zh: 这在这张票上分摊为9.67美元

cues.en: on this particular ticket. The other part of infrastructure,
cues.zh: 基础设施的另一部分，

cues.en: rails, costs Amtrak an additional $3.66
cues.zh: 铁轨，让Amtrak在这张票上额外分摊3.66美元

cues.en: on this ticket. Railroad tracks are extraordinarily
cues.zh: 铁路轨道的建造成本极其

cues.en: expensive to buildtypically
cues.zh: 高昂，通常

cues.en: more than $1,000,000
cues.zh: 每英里超过100万美元

cues.en: per mile, but on routes like DC to New York, they're just used so much that the per train or per ticket cost is negligible.
cues.zh: 但在华盛顿到纽约这样的线路上，使用频率太高，所以每列火车或每张票的成本可以忽略不计。

cues.en: Amtrak is a business so it also needs to pay to run the business. Dollars 2.5
cues.zh: Amtrak是一家企业，所以它也需要为运营付费。2.5美元

cues.en: of this ticket goes to administrative costs and then another 1.31
cues.zh: 这张票的钱用于行政成本，然后还有1.31

cues.en: to advertising.
cues.zh: 用于广告。

cues.en: Moving on, trains are extremely safe compared to cars, but you're still more than three times as likely to be killed on or by a train than a plane. Trains do occasionally crash and they also crash into people. When this happens, Amtrak often has to pay a settlement to the victims and the fees associated with that account for 79¢
cues.zh: 接下来，与汽车相比，火车极其安全，但你因火车而死亡的概率仍比飞机高出三倍以上。火车确实偶尔会出事，也会撞到人。发生这种情况时，Amtrak往往要向受害者支付和解金，相关费用在华盛顿到纽约的票上占79美分

cues.en: on the DC to New York ticket. That does mean that when traveling between DC and New York, in essence, you're paying 79¢
cues.zh: 这意味着，在华盛顿和纽约之间旅行时，本质上，你付了79美分

cues.en: in order for Amtrak to kill or injure people. Those were all the major costs to run a train, but there's still another $5.91
cues.zh: 是为了让Amtrak能够致人死亡或受伤。这些就是运营一列火车的主要成本，但还有另外5.91美元

cues.en: on that ticket that just represents other minor costs.
cues.zh: 这张票只代表了其他一些小额成本。

cues.en: So, the total expense for Amtrak to run that train is $50.14.
cues.zh: 所以，Amtrak 运营那趟列车的总费用是 50.14 美元。

cues.en: The remaining $22.86
cues.zh: 剩下的 22.86 美元

cues.en: is pure profit. You see, the train from DC to New York, the Northeast Regional, is one of the few Amtrak routes to make a profit. The demand, speed, and frequency of the train helps it succeed financially where other routes fail. Per passenger per mile,
cues.zh: 是纯利润。你看，从 DC 到纽约的列车，也就是东北区域号，是 Amtrak 少数盈利的线路之一。这趟列车的需求、速度和频率帮助它在其他线路亏损的情况下实现了财务上的成功。每乘客每英里，

cues.en: Amtrak makes 8¢ of profit on the Northeast Regional, the low speed train, and 29¢
cues.zh: Amtrak 在东北区域号这种低速列车上每乘客每英里赚 8 美分利润，而在 Acela Express 这种高速列车上

cues.en: per passenger mile on the Acela Express, the high speed train. These profitable routes help pay for Amtrak's unprofitable routes and there are a lot of them. Some routes, like the Sunset Limited between New Orleans and Los Angeles, lose as many as 21.7¢
cues.zh: 每乘客每英里赚 29 美分。这些盈利线路帮助支付 Amtrak 亏损线路的费用，而亏损线路有很多。有些线路，比如新奥尔良和洛杉矶之间的日落特快，每乘客每英里亏损高达 21.7 美分

cues.en: per passenger per mile, and when passengers can travel 2,000 miles on that route, that's a lot of loss.
cues.zh: 每位乘客每英里的成本，而当乘客能在该线路上行驶2000英里时，那损失可就大了。

cues.en: As I mentioned, that $49
cues.zh: 正如我提到的，那49美元

cues.en: fare is not the average ticket price to travel between DC and New York. The $49 fare is the price at which Amtrak start selling tickets, but as the date of travel nears, the price can increase to hundreds of dollars. That might seem like price gouging, but it's actually a way to make sure everyone can afford a ticket. That's not to say Amtrak and other train companies are these altruistic organizations trying to bring travel to the masses. It just makes more money. Especially with trains where it costs the operator roughly the same to transport five passengers as it does to transport 500,
cues.zh: 票价并不是往返DC和纽约的平均票价。49美元的票价是Amtrak开始售票时的价格，但随着出行日期临近，价格可能涨到数百美元。这看起来像是价格欺诈，但实际上是一种确保每个人都买得起票的方式。这并不是说Amtrak和其他火车公司是无私的组织，试图让大众都能出行。这只是为了赚更多的钱。尤其是对于火车来说，运送五名乘客和运送500名乘客对运营商的成本大致相同，

cues.en: the operator always wants to have as many seats as possible filled even if that means selling tickets.
cues.zh: 运营商总是希望尽可能填满座位，哪怕这意味着要卖票。

cues.en: In a perfect world for the operator, they could ask every potential passenger what the maximum amount they'd be willing to pay for the journey is. If they adapt the ticket price to every passenger's maximum price, then they can fill each seat with passengers paying the highest possible amount. However, in practice,
cues.zh: 在运营商的理想世界里，他们可以询问每位潜在乘客最多愿意为这趟旅程付多少钱。如果能根据每位乘客的最高心理价位调整票价，就能让每个座位都由支付最高金额的乘客填满。然而，实际上，

cues.en: nobody would ever answer the question truthfully,
cues.zh: 没有人会如实回答这个问题，

cues.en: so it would never work. Ticketing systems, however, try to ask this question subliminally.
cues.zh: 所以这永远行不通。不过，票务系统试图在潜移默化中提出这个问题。

cues.en: Going back to that route from Edinburgh to London, the operator, Virgin Trains East Coast, sells three types of tickets, advance,
cues.zh: 回到那条从爱丁堡到伦敦的线路，运营商Virgin Trains East Coast出售三种车票：预售票、

cues.en: off peak, and anytime. The advance tickets range anywhere from £30 to a £140,
cues.zh: 非高峰票和随时票。预售票价格从30英镑到140英镑不等，

cues.en: the off peak fares cost a £137,
cues.zh: 非高峰票价为137英镑，

cues.en: and the anytime fares cost 148.5.
cues.zh: 随时票价为148.5英镑。

cues.en: For the advanced fares, there are a certain unknown number of tickets at different price levels on sale, and once they're gone, they're gone. For example, there might be 15 tickets at thirty, and once they're sold, the price increases to 35,
cues.zh: 对于预售票，有一定数量的未知车票以不同价格水平出售，一旦售罄就没了。例如，可能有15张30英镑的票，一旦售完，价格就涨到35英镑，

cues.en: then 40, 45, and so on and so forth. That encourages those who can buy early to buy early. Normally, that means tourists.
cues.zh: 然后是40、45，以此类推。这鼓励那些能早买的人尽早购买。通常，这意味着游客。

cues.en: Tourists tend to plan far in advance advance and are more budget conscious since they're paying for their own costs. They're also more likely to travel down to London on the often cheaper plane since they're less attracted by the convenience of the train. These advance fares are only valid for the exact route, day, and time bought which is fine for leisure travelers, but business travelers typically want more flexibility.
cues.zh: 游客往往提前很久做计划，而且更在意预算，因为费用得自己掏。他们也更可能为了便宜坐飞机去伦敦，因为火车的便捷对他们吸引力没那么大。这些预售票只对购买时指定的路线、日期和时间有效，这对休闲旅客没问题，但商务旅客通常想要更多灵活性。

cues.en: Buying advance fares often doesn't work for business travelers since their plans are only made a few weeks or days in advance and since they don't personally pay for their tickets,
cues.zh: 对商务旅客来说，提前买预售票往往行不通，因为他们的行程通常只提前几周甚至几天才定，而且车票也不是自掏腰包，

cues.en: it's no problem for them to pay for the convenience of taking the train on a flexible ticket. That's why they often pay a £148.5
cues.zh: 所以花多点钱买灵活票、图个坐火车方便，对他们来说根本不是问题。这就是为什么他们常常花148.5英镑

cues.en: for an anytime ticket. With these, you can just hop on a train whenever.
cues.zh: 买一张随时票。有了这种票，随时都能上车。

cues.en: It doesn't matter if it's in ten minutes or ten days. You just step on the train and take a seat. The middle ground between those two is the off peak single which lets you take any train that arrives in London after 11:17AM
cues.zh: 不管是十分钟后还是十天后，都没关系。直接上车找个座位就行。介于两者之间的是非高峰单程票，可以乘坐任何在上午11:17之后抵达伦敦的列车，

cues.en: or is on the weekend. These fares are still geared towards business travelers, but by restricting against the early morning trains, they give a discount for those who can avoid the busiest morning trains.
cues.zh: 或者是周末的列车。这些票价仍然面向商务旅客，但通过限制清晨列车，给那些能避开最繁忙早班车的人提供了折扣。

cues.en: For each of these fares there are equivalents in first class.
cues.zh: 这些票价在头等舱都有对应的价格。

cues.en: On top of that, young, disabled, and elderly people get up to one third off their fares with a rail card. That all means that there are essentially 12 different types of tickets for sale and that one person heading to London might be paying £20 while the person sitting right next to them is paying 200, but what they're really paying for is convenience.
cues.zh: 此外，年轻人、残障人士和老年人凭铁路卡最高可享受三分之一的票价优惠。这意味着实际上有12种不同的票在售，一个人去伦敦可能付20英镑，而坐在他旁边的人却付200英镑，但他们真正花钱买的是便利。

cues.en: Now back in The US, if Amtrak only operated profitable routes, their route map would look like this, but the routes that don't make money are the ones that really matter. Amtrak serves over 500 destinations in 46 statesmany
cues.zh: 现在回到美国，如果Amtrak只运营盈利线路，他们的线路图会是这样，但那些不赚钱的线路才是真正重要的。Amtrak服务于46个州的500多个目的地，其中许多

cues.en: of which are small towns with no other means of public transportation.
cues.zh: 是小城镇，没有其他公共交通方式。

cues.en: While trains are normally the more expensive means of transport, they are less expensive than planes to service small communities.
cues.zh: 虽然火车通常是比较昂贵的交通方式，但服务小型社区的成本比飞机低。

cues.en: The small airports in the rural parts of America are extraordinarily
cues.zh: 美国乡村地区的小型机场运营成本极其高昂。

cues.en: expensive to operate. Even if there are just two or three flights a day, they still need a runway, terminal, security, and air traffic control while a rural train station needs barely any infrastructure or maintenance.
cues.zh: 哪怕一天只有两三趟航班，它们依然需要跑道、航站楼、安检和空中交通管制，而乡村火车站几乎不需要什么基础设施或维护。

cues.en: In fact, it's cheaper to fly from Chicago
cues.zh: 事实上，从芝加哥飞往

cues.en: to London than it is to fly from Havre, Montana to Chicago whereas Amtrak brings passengers from Havre to Chicago for only a few $100.
cues.zh: 伦敦比从蒙大拿州哈弗尔飞往芝加哥还便宜，而Amtrak把乘客从哈弗尔送到芝加哥只要几百美元。

cues.en: Much more in budget for the average resident of Havre who makes only 22,000
cues.zh: 对哈弗市的普通居民来说，这更在预算之内，他们每年只挣22000

cues.en: per year. Of course this is a political issue, but a part of why trains are so expensive is to allow train operators to fulfill obligations to serve small communities who need solid transport links. Research has shown that ease of access to transport has a stronger influence on whether someone will earn more than their parents did than the level of crime in their area or whether they grew up in a two parent household, and so keeping trains running through rural America is incredibly important.
cues.zh: 美元。当然这是个政治问题，但火车票价之所以这么贵，部分原因是为了让铁路运营商履行义务，服务那些需要可靠交通连接的小社区。研究表明，相比所在地区的犯罪率或是否在双亲家庭长大，交通便利程度对一个人能否比父母挣得更多影响更大，因此保持列车穿行于美国乡村至关重要。

cues.en: Next time you take the train from DC to New York, just keep in mind that that $22.86
cues.zh: 下次你坐火车从DC去纽约时，记住那22.86美元的利润

cues.en: of profit goes to making sure that someone from Havre can get to Chicago for less than you can fly to Europe.
cues.zh: 是为了确保有人能从哈弗尔去到芝加哥，花费比飞往欧洲还少。
